blogPosts.title: How Much Does Hot Water System Replacement Cost in Melbourne in 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: Considering a new hot water system in Melbourne? We break down the cost of electric, gas, solar and heat pump replacements in Southbank and surrounding suburbs.
body: Hot water system replacement is one of the most common plumbing jobs in Melbourne homes. Whether your old electric storage unit has finally given out or you want to upgrade to a more efficient gas continuous flow system, knowing what you'll pay upfront helps you budget. In Southbank and across Melbourne, prices can vary based on the type of system, the complexity of installation, and whether you need a same-day service.

For a standard electric hot water system replacement in Melbourne, you can expect to pay between $800 and $1,500 including installation. Gas storage systems typically range from $1,200 to $2,000, while gas continuous flow units cost anywhere from $1,500 to $3,000. Solar and heat pump systems are more expensive upfront — between $3,000 and $6,000 — but they offer lower running costs and government rebates that can cut the initial price significantly.

Installation costs also depend on your existing setup. If you're switching from electric to gas, you'll need a gas line run to the unit, which adds $300–$800. Upgrading from a storage tank to a continuous flow system may require new pipework and flue modifications. At Mr Emergency Plumbing Melbourne, we factor all these details into a fixed, written quote before any work begins, so there are no surprises.

Rebates and incentives can make a big difference in the final price. The Victorian Energy Upgrades (VEU) program offers discounts on energy-efficient heat pump systems, and the Solar Homes Program provides rebates for solar hot water installations. Our team can help you navigate the paperwork and ensure you receive the maximum savings. In many cases, the rebate can cover up to half the cost of a heat pump system.

Labour costs in Melbourne are generally consistent across the city, but expect to pay more for emergency weekend or public holiday installations. Mr Emergency Plumbing charges the same rates 24/7 — no overtime premiums. Our vans carry common hot water units from Rheem, Rinnai, and Bosch, so we can install a replacement on the same day you call, often within hours.

If your hot water system is over ten years old, starts leaking or produces rusty water, it's time to consider a replacement. Delaying can lead to flooding and property damage. Call Mr Emergency Plumbing Melbourne for a free quote and fast installation. We serve Southbank, the CBD, Werribee, Sunbury and the entire Mornington Peninsula.

blogPosts.title: Top 5 Signs Your Blocked Drain Needs a CCTV Camera Inspection
blogPosts.excerpt: Is your drain slow or gurgling? Learn when to call for a CCTV camera inspection in Melbourne and how it saves you money on unnecessary excavation.
body: A blocked drain can start as a slow sink and escalate into a sewage overflow if left untreated. Melbourne homes, especially older ones in Southbank and inner suburbs, often struggle with tree root intrusion and collapsed pipes. While a plunger or chemical cleaner might offer temporary relief, a permanent fix requires knowing the exact cause. That's where CCTV drain camera inspections come in.

A CCTV drain inspection involves a waterproof camera attached to a flexible rod that travels through your pipes. It sends live footage to a monitor, allowing plumbers to see blockages, cracks, root masses, and pipe misalignment in real time. In Melbourne, we use this technology to avoid digging up your yard or driveway unnecessarily. Instead, we target the problem area precisely.

So, when should you ask for a CCTV inspection? The first sign is a drain that's frequently blocked despite your best efforts. If you find yourself unblocking the kitchen sink or shower drain every few weeks, there's likely a deeper issue. Second, if you notice gurgling sounds when water runs — especially in toilets or sinks — that indicates trapped air caused by a partial blockage.

Third, multiple fixtures draining slowly at the same time suggests a main line problem, not just a local blockage. Fourth, foul odours coming from drains indicate decomposing waste caught in a pipe crack or root intrusion. Finally, if your drains back up after heavy rain, you may have collapsed or misaligned pipes. Any of these signs warrant a professional camera inspection.

The cost of a CCTV drain inspection in Melbourne typically ranges from $150 to $350. At Mr Emergency Plumbing, we often include the inspection as part of our drain cleaning service. The inspection footage helps us decide between hydro-jet cleaning, pipe relining, or excavation. Pipe relining is a popular trenchless solution that can fix cracked pipes without digging.

Preventative CCTV inspections are also a smart investment for property managers and homeowners. Having a visual record of your pipes can help you plan maintenance and avoid emergency call-outs. If you've noticed any of these signs at your Southbank or Melbourne property, contact Mr Emergency Plumbing. Our team will send a camera down your drains and provide a clear report with a fixed price for any needed repairs.

blogPosts.title: Emergency Plumbing in Southbank: What to Do While You Wait for the Plumber
blogPosts.excerpt: A plumbing emergency in Southbank? Here's exactly what to do to minimise damage before Mr Emergency arrives within 30 minutes.
body: A burst pipe or overflowing toilet can cause thousands of dollars in water damage in minutes. If you're in Southbank or anywhere in Melbourne, knowing what to do while waiting for an emergency plumber can save your furniture, floors and peace of mind. At Mr Emergency Plumbing, we aim for a 30-minute response, but those minutes count. Follow these steps to stay safe and limit damage.

First, locate your main water shut-off valve. In most Melbourne homes, it's under the kitchen sink or near the front of the property on the water meter. Turn it clockwise to stop all water flow. If the emergency is isolated — say a burst pipe under the sink — you can turn off the local valve instead. But if you can't find a local valve, shut off the main one. This stops the flooding instantly.

Second, turn off your hot water system. If the leak is on the hot water line, your system will keep trying to heat water that's spilling out. For electric systems, switch off the circuit breaker. For gas systems, turn the thermostat to 'off' or 'pilot' and shut the gas valve if safe. This prevents damage to your unit and reduces the risk of gas leaks.

Third, open taps to relieve pressure. Once the water is shut off, open a cold water tap at the lowest point in the house (usually outside or in the garage) and one at the highest point (like an upstairs bathroom). This drains residual water from the pipes and reduces pressure on the broken section, minimising further leakage.

Fourth, start cleaning up standing water. Use towels, a mop, or a wet/dry vacuum to remove water from floors and baseboards. If you have a basement or timber floors, get the water up quickly to prevent rotting and mould. Move any furniture or valuables out of the affected area. The faster you dry surfaces, the less permanent damage you'll have.

Finally, call Mr Emergency Plumbing Melbourne on 1300 164 064. Give us a clear description of the problem and your Southbank address. Our plumber will arrive within 30 minutes with a fully stocked van and a fixed price for the repair. We'll stop the leak, assess any damage, and get your plumbing back to normal — all with no overtime charges.

blogPosts.title: Gas Leak Detection in Melbourne: What Every Homeowner Should Know
blogPosts.excerpt: Smell gas in your Melbourne home? Learn how to detect a gas leak safely — and when to call a licensed gas fitter like Mr Emergency Plumbing.
body: A gas leak in Melbourne is a serious emergency that requires immediate action. Natural gas is odourless in its raw form, but gas companies add a sulphur-like smell (similar to rotten eggs) to help you detect it. If you notice this smell in your home or business in Southbank or anywhere in Melbourne, do not ignore it. Even a small leak can lead to fire, explosion, or carbon monoxide poisoning.

The first thing to do if you suspect a gas leak is to stop using any electrical appliances. Do not flip light switches, use your phone, or operate any electronics — even a tiny spark can ignite gas. Open doors and windows to ventilate the area, and get everyone out of the building. If you can safely reach the gas meter, turn off the gas supply valve (it's usually a lever near the meter).

The second step is to evacuate and call a licensed gas fitter immediately. Mr Emergency Plumbing Melbourne offers 24/7 gas leak detection and repair. Our gas fitters are fully licensed and trained to find leaks using electronic gas detectors and soap-and-water tests. We'll locate the source — whether it's a loose fitting, a corroded pipe, or a faulty appliance — and fix it on the spot.

Common signs of a gas leak beyond the smell include hissing sounds near gas appliances or pipes, dead plants or grass near a gas line, bubbles in standing water, and higher-than-normal gas bills. You might also experience physical symptoms like headaches, dizziness, nausea or fatigue if you've been exposed to a slow leak. Carbon monoxide detectors are recommended for Melbourne homes with gas appliances.

After a gas leak repair, it's important to have your gas system tested to ensure there are no other issues. Our gas fitters perform a full pressure test and check all appliances for correct operation. We also offer carbon monoxide testing to make sure your home is safe. Regular gas appliance servicing can prevent leaks from developing in the first place.

If you ever smell gas in your Southbank or Melbourne home, evacuate and call 1300 164 064. Mr Emergency Plumbing will arrive within 30 minutes, fix the leak, and test your system — all with a fixed upfront price. Don't take risks with gas. Call the experts who treat every emergency with the seriousness it deserves.
